description: Table 4 is a single rendered table image (no plots, micrographs or schematics), titled "The elements fraction and Ms, Md30 temperature". It has six columns — Specimen, C^a (mass%), Mn^b (mass%), Al^b (mass%), M_s (°C), M_d30 (°C) — and three data rows for the solution-treated specimens H70, H80 and H90. H70: C 0.556 mass%, Mn 8.91 mass%, Al 5.22 mass%, M_s 33 °C, M_d30 168 °C. H80: C 0.479, Mn 8.85, Al 5.1, M_s 67 °C, M_d30 204 °C. H90: C 0.391, Mn 8.34, Al 4.67, M_s 120 °C, M_d30 249 °C. The superscripts a and b are defined in the citing text (C from XRD analysis, Mn and Al from EDS analysis), not inside the table. Read together, the rows show that as C, Mn and Al contents decrease monotonically from H70 to H90, both M_s and M_d30 rise monotonically, reaching 120 °C and 249 °C in H90. The table therefore supplies the compositional basis for the argument that lower C in austenite destabilises it, raising M_s/M_d30 and enabling strain-induced martensitic transformation (TRIP). One numerical inconsistency exists: the citing text quotes M_d30 = 268 °C for H70, whereas the table prints 168 °C.

observations.observation: The table's header row reads: Specimen, C^a (mass%), Mn^b (mass%), Al^b (mass%), M_s (°C), M_d30 (°C).
Row H70 lists C 0.556 mass%, Mn 8.91 mass%, Al 5.22 mass%, M_s 33 °C and M_d30 168 °C.
Row H80 lists C 0.479 mass%, Mn 8.85 mass%, Al 5.1 mass%, M_s 67 °C and M_d30 204 °C.
Row H90 lists C 0.391 mass%, Mn 8.34 mass%, Al 4.67 mass%, M_s 120 °C and M_d30 249 °C.
Across H70 to H90 the C, Mn and Al contents decrease monotonically while both M_s and M_d30 increase monotonically, the highest temperatures being those of H90.
The table title printed with the figure is 'The elements fraction and M_s, M_d30 temperature'.
The caption states the table gives the elements fraction and the M_s and M_d30 temperatures of the specimens.
The citing text states that C content was measured from XRD analysis and Mn and Al contents from EDS analysis (footnote superscripts a and b).

The citing text states that M_s is the martensitic transformation starting temperature and M_d30 is the temperature at which 50% of austenite has transformed into martensite at a true strain of 30%, with elemental contents in mass percentage.
The citing text states the calculated M_s and M_d30 values were 120 °C and 249 °C for H90, 67 °C and 204 °C for H80, and 33 °C and 268 °C for H70, quoting Eqs. (2) and (3).
Discrepancy: the citing text quotes M_d30 = 268 °C for H70, but the table itself prints 168 °C for H70; both readings are reported here and the visual reading of the table is favoured.

The citing text concludes that lower C content makes austenite metastable and enables martensite transformation in these steels, attributing the higher H90 temperatures to its lower C and Mn contents.
